acceptance: The downstream contract check refuses a carried patch that has a hunk whose added lines are all blank, and passes on every patch currently on main.
The check refuses the old patch downstream/patches/sqlite-date-extraction.patch from commit 860a2bce7.
Either the step that wrote the hunk is identified and fixed with a refresh test reproducing it, or the context records that it could not be reproduced within the time-box and what was tried.
context:
Decision gate: time-box the root-cause search (about half a day of effort) by rebuilding the v30.30.0 refresh from its recorded inputs. If it does not reproduce, ship the contract check alone and record the attempt; no owner decision is needed for that path.

Verification rubric: (1) the new check fails on the 860a2bce7 patch and passes on main; (2) downstream refresh and contract tests pass; (3) if a cause is fixed, a refresh test that produced the blank-only hunk passes after the fix.

Guardrails: do not hand-edit normalized patches on main to satisfy the check; the check must not reject hunks that add blank lines alongside real changes; no change to patch application order or the manifest schema.
description: After the v30.30.0 refresh (860a2bce7), downstream/patches/sqlite-date-extraction.patch ended with hunk '@@ -287,6 +381,10 @@' that adds four blank lines after dateadd_sql and nothing else; source commit 34cd3e9f has no such hunk. It anchored the patch on the lines where upstream v30.31.0 later added datesub_sql and was the first conflict git reported in issue #88. The hand refresh (#89) regenerated the patch without it, so main is clean now, but the cause was not traced and a later refresh can produce it again.
